terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; with cum and the ablative, or the dative
terms.comment: From compār, “matched”: not the same word as comparō, “get ready”, which Lewis & Short gives as a separate entry. A comparison is comparātiō (Traupman 294).

terms.grammar: verb, irregular (like ferō); with cum and the ablative, or the dative
evidence: Phaedr. 4.25.3: cōnferre nostrīs tū potes tē laudibus?

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation; with an accusative and a dative
terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Acc., Verg., Ov.
evidence: Verg. G. 4.176: sī parva licet compōnere magnīs
Verg. E. 1.23: sīc parvīs compōnere magna solēbam

phrases.english: if one may compare small things with great

phrases.latin: formīca et musca contendēbant ācriter quae plūris esset. musca sīc coepit prior: cōnferre nostrīs tū potes tē laudibus?
phrases.english: The ant and the fly were arguing hotly which was worth more. The fly began: “Can you compare yourself with my merits?”

phrases.latin: Hunc pānem cum illō cōnfer: uter tibi magis placet?
phrases.english: Compare this bread with that one: which do you like better?

sources: Lewis & Short: comparo · Lewis & Short: confero · Lewis & Short: compono
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 294.
